newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran, Yugoslavia vow to improve ties after tension.
newsitem.headline: Iran, Yugoslavia vow to improve ties after tension.

text.p: Iran and Yugoslavia pledged on Thursday to mend their diplomatic and trade ties damaged by years of tension over the conflict in Bosnia, the Iranian news agency IRNA said.

It said Yugoslav Foreign Trade Minister Borislav Vukovic and Iranian Economy and Finance Minister Morteza Mohammadkhan signed a memorandum of understanding in Tehran calling for better political and economic ties.
Vukovic's five-day visit came after years of tension between his country and the Islamic republic which has strongly backed Bosnia's Moslem-led government in the conflict in the former Yugoslavia.
Vukovic said his visit "was aimed at reviving bilateral relations" and called for reconvening in October the two countries' joint economic commission which has not met since 1990, the agency said.
Iran and the former Yugoslavia had strong economic ties and cooperated closely in the Non-Allied Movement before the outbreak of the Balkan conflict.
Serbia and its tiny ally Montenegro make up the new Yugoslavia formed after the violent break-up of the former six-member Balkan state in 1991.

Vukovic earlier met Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati who told him "the Iranian people's feelings had been severely harmed by ethnic cleansing in Bosnia", but added that Tehran supported peace and cooperation between all ethnic groups.
